match.reason: No bank point teaches grasslands being used for grazing and grain while facing drought and soil erosion; the closest, geo-bush-foods-changed-biomes, is about bush foods and Indigenous food, and the others cover general biome food, definitions or productivity.

draft.title: Grassland biomes and food
card: A grassland is a biome where grasses are the main plants and there are few trees. Rainfall is too low for forest but usually enough for grass.

Grasslands, such as the Australian rangelands and the North American prairies, are used for food. Livestock graze on the grass, and the deeper soils of some areas are used to grow grain crops such as wheat.
Grasslands face drought, which is a long period of low rainfall. Dry spells can leave little grass for animals and cause crops to fail.
They also face soil erosion, which is the wearing away and removal of topsoil by wind or water. Too many animals or bare, ploughed ground can leave soil open to erosion.
draft.remember: Grasslands feed people through grazing and grain, but drought and soil erosion put that food production at risk.

a.q: Which pair of uses best describes how grassland biomes help to supply food?
opts: Grazing livestock and growing grain crops
Fishing in rivers and farming in rainforests
a.why: Grasslands are mainly used for grazing animals and, where soils allow, growing grain such as wheat. Timber and fishing are not the main food uses of grasslands, and the card does not give medicines or carbon storage as their food uses.
a.clue: Think about what grows on grassland and what eats it.

b.q: Jess grazes cattle on a grassland property in western Queensland. After a long dry spell, strong winds blow away bare topsoil. Which problems is she facing?
opts: Soil erosion only, as drought is a wet-season problem
Drought only, as wind does not move soil
Flooding and loss of grass from too much rain
b.why: A long period of low rainfall is drought, and the wind carrying away bare topsoil is soil erosion. She faces both, and each can make the other problem harder to manage. The other options deny one problem or describe rain that the scenario does not mention.
b.clue: Name what the dry spell is, then name what the wind is doing to the soil.

a.best: Grazing livestock and growing grain crops
